candidate_claim_transitions.notes: Worker repair 2026-09-04, verbatim record results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/evidence/data_budget/repair_o28.txt. WHAT WAS DONE, per defect. (1) Parser: load_budget now strips the surrounding quote BEFORE matching the shell-default form and drops an inline trailing comment after the closing quote - testing val.startswith('${') on the still-quoted string was the whole defect. It resolves ${NAME:-default} to the FILE's default branch and deliberately does not consult os.environ, so the fix cannot be used as a new environment channel. `python3 prune_retention.py` with no --root now dry-runs the mission root /scratch/schmidt/ssci-anima/ssci-haiyangw/ktg-train (contract case S1), which is exactly the call written in the scratch_guard.sh header; the header contract was left calling the pruner without --root and now matches what works. (2) Vector decisions. PINNED: budget.env and the three fixtures now hold literal values, so sourcing overwrites any exported KTG_SCRATCH_ROOT or KTG_CYCLE_PROJECTED_BYTES (cases L, P); the guard REFUSES a constants file that does not resolve inside its own directory, which closes the loose-KTG_BUDGET_ENV vector (cases N1/N2); the guard also refuses an in-tree constants file whose KTG_* assignments contain a ${...} indirection, so the file cannot be rewritten into a form that re-opens the environment channel (case O). DOCUMENTED AS CALLER CONTROL, stated in the scratch_guard.sh header and in the amended claim: --projected-bytes N (that is the guard's input; --projected-bytes 0 does make the projection 0, case M), --root DIR (a re-scoped run now prints a NOTE naming the constants file's root so it cannot pass unremarked in a cycle log, case Q), and KTG_QUOTAS_BIN (it cannot LOOSEN anything because the guard takes min(quotas.py, df -B1): a fake reporter claiming 99999.00 TB free is discarded in favour of live df and the group floor still aborts, case R). The pruner takes the same out-of-tree refusal on --budget-env / KTG_BUDGET_ENV (case S4) and ignores an exported KTG_SCRATCH_ROOT (case S3). Contract now 25/25 (11 pre-existing A-K unchanged + 12 new o28 cases + 2 cases T1/T2 for a second defect found while repairing, below). Every new negative case is paired with a positive control that takes the other branch, so none can pass without reaching its assertion. ADDITIONALLY, a second defect surfaced while running the repaired contract and is fixed in the same change: a single non-zero `du -sb` (an entry vanishing from under the walk on a live mission root) was read as 'cannot measure', so scratch_guard.sh exited 3 and would have aborted a healthy production cycle. A non-zero du is now retried (KTG_DU_ATTEMPTS, default 3, KTG_DU_RETRY_SLEEP 2 s) in both scratch_guard.sh and prune_retention.py rolling mode, and its partial total is still discarded because a partial total under-counts; a persistently unreadable root still exits 3 (cases T1/T2). candidate_amended_result_row.claim: codes/data_budget/scratch_guard.sh refuses, with a non-zero exit, any cycle whose declared projected write would take du -sb of the measured root past 536870912000 B (exit 1) or that would start while group scratch free space, taken as min(quotas.py, df -B1), is below 1099511627776 B (exit 2). Its byte thresholds, its default per-cycle projection and its default root come only from a constants FILE that must resolve inside the guard's own directory and must hold literal values; a file elsewhere, or an in-tree file containing a ${...} indirection, is refused with exit 3. In consequence no environment variable can loosen the guard: KTG_SCRATCH_HARD_BYTES, KTG_SCRATCH_ROOT, KTG_CYCLE_PROJECTED_BYTES and KTG_BUDGET_ENV are each demonstrated inert, and KTG_QUOTAS_BIN cannot raise the measured free space because the guard takes the minimum with live df. What remains caller control, by design and stated in the guard's own header: --projected-bytes N (the caller declares the bytes its cycle will write; 0 means 0) and --root DIR (a root differing from the constants file's is announced with a NOTE line in the cycle log). A `du -sb` that exits non-zero - routine when an entry vanishes from under the walk on a live root - is retried rather than read as 'cannot measure', but its partial total is never used, because a partial total under-counts and an unreadable subtree would otherwise hide usage from the cap; a root that keeps failing still exits 3. codes/data_budget/prune_retention.py, called with no --root exactly as the guard's header contract writes it, resolves the mission root from the same constants file and bounds retention to longterm_checkpoints <= 6, rejectedmodels <= 10, selfplay <= 3 generations, scripts/dated <= 3 and shuffleddata <= 3 windows older than 2 h, sweeps orphan .tmp windows, prints its protected set before any path becomes a candidate, is dry-run unless --apply, and in --target-bytes rolling mode never drops below one shuffle window plus one selfplay generation nor removes a generation newer than the oldest retained window. Measured on login03 the mission root is 7.56e9 B, far under the cap. Everything here is measured on the guard artefacts (a 25-case fixture-driven exit-code contract in which every negative case is paired with a positive control, synthetic retention trees, pre-loop du); production behaviour is still not measured, because no wrapper calls the guard yet.

The 1 TiB group free-space floor is a design choice, not a measurement: it is 2x the mission's whole 500 GiB budget.

quotas.py reports DECIMAL TB (40.00 TB matches the 40000000000000 B pool df reports), is rounded to 0.01 TB and refreshed hourly; the guard takes min(quotas.py, df -B1). Conservative in the direction that matters: a stale-low quotas.py can only refuse spuriously, and a fast fill is caught by live df.
